newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Q1 1997 aluminium premiums set around $62.
newsitem.headline: Japan Q1 1997 aluminium premiums set around $62.

text.p: Premiums for aluminium shipments to Japan in the first quarter of 1997 were being set around $62 per tonne over London Metal Exchange cash prices, steady with this year's fourth quarter, market sources said on Tuesday.
Foreign producers and Japanese trade houses agreed on the premiums by the end of last week, they said.

"Foreign producers originally wanted to set the premiums at about $65 a tonne," a major trade house official said. "But considering high aluminium stocks in Japan, they agreed to make a compromise," he said.
Aluminium stocks at the port of Yokohama, west of Tokyo, are currently at about 250,000 tonnes, the traders said. The Yokohama port's aluminium stocks account for 70 percent of total stocks in Japan.
